Conduct equipment criticality assessments to prioritize assets based on safety, operational impact, failure probability, and replacement costs. Develop risk-based maintenance strategies that balance equipment availability, maintenance expenditure, operational requirements, and safety. Analyze equipment failure data to identify recurring issues, underlying causes, and opportunities for corrective action. Lead or support root cause analysis (RCA) investigations involving equipment breakdowns, performance degradation, and recurring operational failures. Apply structured problem-solving methodologies to determine failure mechanisms and prevent repeated equipment incidents. Develop and implement corrective and preventive actions based on investigation findings and reliability assessments. Review maintenance records, inspection reports, equipment histories, and technical documentation to evaluate asset condition and reliability trends. Establish and optimize preventive maintenance programs based on equipment criticality, manufacturer recommendations, operating environments, and historical performance. Support predictive maintenance initiatives using condition monitoring, vibration analysis, thermography, oil analysis, ultrasonic testing, and other applicable diagnostic techniques. Evaluate condition monitoring results and recommend timely maintenance interventions to prevent unexpected failures. Collaborate with maintenance planning teams to improve maintenance schedules, inspection intervals, and work execution strategies. Review maintenance procedures and identify opportunities to eliminate unnecessary tasks while preserving equipment reliability and safety. Develop reliability-centered maintenance (RCM) strategies for critical equipment and operational systems. Apply failure mode and effects analysis (FMEA) and failure mode, effects, and criticality analysis (FMECA) where appropriate. Conduct failure probability assessments and evaluate the operational consequences of equipment degradation. Support reliability, availability, and maintainability (RAM) studies for new and existing assets. Monitor mean time between failures (MTBF), mean time to repair (MTTR), equipment availability, and other reliability indicators. Analyze downtime trends and identify the major contributors to lost production, service interruptions, and maintenance expenditure. Prepare reliability dashboards, technical reports, performance summaries, and recommendations for management review. Develop equipment performance models and use historical data to identify emerging reliability risks. Evaluate equipment operating parameters to identify abnormal conditions, inefficiencies, and potential failure precursors. Work with engineering teams to assess equipment design weaknesses and recommend modifications that improve maintainability and reliability. Review equipment specifications, technical drawings, operating manuals, and maintenance requirements to identify reliability concerns. Participate in equipment selection, technical evaluations, and lifecycle planning for new installations and replacement assets. Review commissioning results and equipment acceptance documentation to ensure reliability requirements are addressed before operational handover.
